text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The clemency commission headed by the President Algirdas Brazauskas considered 85 appeals on Wednesday and 29 will be satisfied.
- State security department officials detained a group of five people suspected of forgery of various official documents.
- Three deputy culture ministers submitted letters of resignation. They dissaproved of the lack of a clear culture policy.
- Television tube producer Ekranas will have to sack 500 out of 6400 emploees after the company upgraded its lines.
- Vilfima was the most active brokerage house in May with turnover of over 37 million litas.
- The Bank of Lithuania is to decide today whether to extend the 14.1 million litas credit term for Tauras Bank's liquidity problems.
- The confederation of industrialists urged the ruling Homeland Union party not to raise energy prices.
- The Bank of Lithuania held its first repo auction on Wednesday. The central bank purchased government T-bills for 300,000 litas with a seven-day maturity and seven percent interest rate.
- The government plans a budget deficit in 1998 of a maximum 600 million litas or 1.4 percent of GDP.
